package_info.package_versions: unknown (specific version not stated, but an old version in use)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was maliciously modified by attackers who appended JavaScript code to the end of the legitimate modernizr library. This injected code was designed to intercept sensitive payment form data (including credit card numbers, expiration dates, and CVVs) and exfiltrate it to an attacker-controlled domain. The modification transformed a trusted library into a vehicle for a Magecart-style supply chain attack, enabling large-scale theft of payment information from users.

execution_context.trigger: When the payment form is loaded and a user submits payment information on the affected website
execution_context.file_location: modernizr.js (malicious code appended to the end of the legitimate library, served from the compromised BA web server)
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form field values
Ability to initiate outbound HTTP requests to external domains

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The injected code attaches an event listener to the payment form. When a user submits the form, it programmatically collects the entered credit card number, expiration date, and CVV from the form fields. It then encodes this sensitive data using base64 (via btoa) and sends it to an attacker-controlled server by creating a new image request, effectively exfiltrating the payment information without user knowledge.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code covertly intercepts sensitive payment data from the form and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is characteristic of web skimming (Magecart) attacks and is not expected in any legitimate JavaScript library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate modernizr.js library should only perform feature detection and should never access or interact with payment forms, nor should it transmit user data to external domains. The presence of code that hooks into payment form submission and exfiltrates raw payment data is a clear and severe violation of expected library behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts for analytics or fraud detection may monitor form events or validate input, but they do not collect and transmit full payment card details to untrusted or unknown domains. Any such exfiltration of raw payment data is highly abnormal and indicative of malicious intent.
key_indicators: Injected code appended to a trusted third-party library (modernizr.js)
Direct access to payment form fields (e.g., input[name=cardnumber], input[name=exp], input[name=cvv])
Outbound HTTP request to an untrusted, attacker-controlled domain (e.g., malicious-domain.com) upon form submission
Use of base64 encoding (btoa) to obfuscate exfiltrated data
No user notification or consent for data collection and transmission
Event listener attached specifically to payment form submission

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits an unpatched Magento vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to the British Airways web server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains the ability to modify static assets served to website users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker appends malicious JavaScript code to the end of the modernizr.js library file on the compromised server.
attack_chain.leads_to: The tainted modernizr.js file is served to all users accessing the payment page.

attack_chain.action: When a user loads the payment page, the browser executes the malicious code embedded in modernizr.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: The code attaches an event listener to the payment form, monitoring for form submission.

attack_chain.action: Upon form submission, the malicious code collects the user's payment details and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card data in real time.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected JavaScript code appended to or modifying trusted libraries such as modernizr.js
JavaScript accessing payment form fields (e.g., card number, expiration, CVV) and transmitting data to external domains
Outbound network requests (e.g., image or beacon requests) triggered specifically on payment form submission to non-whitelisted or unknown domains
Use of encoding functions (e.g., btoa) immediately prior to network exfiltration
file_indicators: modernizr.js file with appended or altered code not matching the official release hash or content
Presence of unfamiliar or unauthorized <script> tags or inline event listeners on payment pages
Static asset files (e.g., modernizr.js) with increased file size or unexpected code at the end
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests from payment pages to domains not associated with the organization (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual image or beacon requests initiated during payment form submission events
Network traffic containing base64-encoded payloads in query parameters sent to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and verify the integrity of static assets by comparing deployed files (e.g., modernizr.js) against known-good hashes or official releases. Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict outbound requests from payment pages to only trusted domains. Inspect JavaScript on payment pages for unauthorized event listeners or code accessing sensitive form fields. Monitor network traffic for requests to untrusted domains, especially those containing encoded data during payment form submissions. Set up alerts for any changes to static assets or the appearance of new/unexpected script tags on sensitive pages.
